title: SparseLoRA: Accelerating LLM Fine-Tuning with Contextual Sparsity
summary: Pinned sparse linear operations detach selected base-path gradients. Major for released core implementation; historical results attribution remains Needs Evidence. Table4 all-category caption is contradicted by three displayed entries.
limitations: No author code executed; no PyTorch runtime test (not installed in active Python).
Historical correspondence and actual repaired performance unknown.
Raw timing and run-level uncertainty unverified.
Table3 average appears to omit WNLI; convention unclear.

problems.title: Selected base projections lose their backward Jacobian

source_claim.paraphrase: Sparse selected-weight loss and gradient computation with dense adapters.

assumptions: Enabled sparse PEFT base projection; proper channel subset
Frozen base weight; input depends on upstream trainable parameter
Indices fixed locally; no derivative through top-k required
problems.check: Registry selects out_scatter/in_gather; activation gather/scatter occurs in no_grad. With x(theta)=(theta,0), W=diag(2,3), selected0, loss=.5||y||^2, correct derivative at1 is4; detachment removes this branch contribution and gives0. Independent rational finite difference=4.
problems.result: Release omits selected frozen-base contributions to upstream gradients.
counterevidence: Dense LoRA, dense tokens and residual paths still learn.
No historical commit/run log links these exact lines to printed results.
Deliberate stop-gradient would be a distinct approximation needing disclosure.
problems.core_dependency: Core sparse-training mechanism and interpretation of backward-computation savings.
problems.impact: Major released implementation defect; historical accuracy and speed effects remain Needs Evidence, not demonstrated benchmark damage.

correction.statement: Keep activation gather/scatter differentiable while masks/indices may be predicted without gradients. Re-measure accuracy and speed before claiming repaired equivalence.
